wins.text: Full year adjusted EPS up 19% YoY, delivered towards the higher end of original guidance range despite revenue down ~3% (~$2.5B)
Ground delivered highest adjusted operating income in company history for both Q4 and full year; Q4 adjusted operating margin expanded 130 bps with operating income up $133M YoY
Achieved $1.8B DRIVE structural cost savings target in FY24, one year ahead of the $4B FY25 cumulative target; CapEx-to-revenue target of <6.5% also hit one year early
Returned nearly $4B to stockholders in FY24, including $2.5B in share repurchases ($500M above plan) and a 10% dividend increase; adjusted free cash flow of $4.1B, up ~$500M YoY
ROIC improved 120 bps to 9.9%; Freight Q4 operating income up $58M with margins up 220 bps despite soft demand environment

risks.text: USPS contract expiration on September 29 creates a $500M operating profit headwind in FY25, concentrated in Q2 with mitigation efforts ramping in Q3+

International export yield pressure of $400M expected in FY25 as pandemic-era demand surcharges diminish and mix shifts toward deferred services; increased global air cargo capacity adding further pressure

Express adjusted operating income fell $92M and margins declined 90 bps in Q4, pressured by lower international yield, higher purchased transportation costs from Tricolor launch, and incentive comp headwinds
Two fewer operating days in FY25 vs FY24 reduces profitability by ~$300M — a calendar dynamic not seen since FY2001
Network 2.0 and One FedEx integration carry execution risk; analysts explicitly raised historical precedent of failed network integrations (e.g., TNT) as a concern

guidance_items.detail: FY25 adjusted EPS guided to $20–$22 (midpoint $21), implying ~12%–24% growth vs FY24 adjusted EPS; prior year delivered $19 range
FY25 revenue expected to grow low to mid-single digits YoY, driven by improving U.S. domestic parcel and international export demand; prior year revenue was down 3%
Adjusted operating income expected to increase ~15% YoY at midpoint ($7.2B), driven by $2.2B incremental DRIVE savings more than offsetting $1.3B+ in headwinds
FY25 CapEx guided to $5.2B, down YoY as % of revenue; aircraft CapEx targeted at ~$1B in FY26
FY25 share repurchases planned at $2.5B including $1B in Q1; dividend increased 10% on top of prior year's 10% increase

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Potential spin-off or sale of FedEx Freight LTL business and downstream implications for Tricolor network strategy
Network integration execution risk citing historical failures (e.g., TNT acquisition)
Tariff/trade policy risk and concentration in China-based e-commerce customers as a percentage of revenue
